messages:
ravi: Starting onboarding for Newt customer's LoRA adapter (newt-lora@v0.9) into staging. Objective: token-map check, small behavioral eval (90 convs), int8 vs int4 quant comparison, and a calibration sweep. Tagging @lina for tokenizer concerns.

lina: Got it. Uploading eval pack: gs://redwood-evals/newt/mini-pack-2026-03-23.tar.gz — includes 30 currency examples, 15 invoice templates, 10 long threads.

ravi: Running token map diff first. Command: python tools/tokenmap_diff.py --base open-7b --adapter newt-lora --out /tmp/newt-map.json; expect custom-v1 vocab. Will notify if OOVs > 0.

eval-bot: tokenmap check completed: remapped=7, oovs=1. Details: /ci/artifacts/newt/tokenmap.json

joel: One OOV is the "ORDR" token variant we've seen. If it's only formatting we can remap to "ORDER". Pinged adapter author to confirm.

frank: Also note Newt adapter adds a soft-prompt prefix for invoice parsing; soft-prompt can shift token alignments. Consider running a soft-prompt free baseline.

ravi: Good call. I'll run baseline (adapter but without soft-prompt) then full adapter. Baseline run queued job=job_99801.

eval-bot: baseline run done. metrics: numeric-MAE=1.05, money-format-f1=0.97, p50latency +6ms. Full adapter +int4 quant run queued next.

lina: Running int4 calibrated sweep (--quant-mode calibrated-symmetric, n-calib=512) and int8 standard for comparison. Please flag any examples where adapter-only fails but baseline passes.

ravi: First int4 pass results: numeric-MAE=1.9, money-format-f1=0.89, edge-case decimal collapse seen on ~3/30 currency cases. Int8 report: numeric-MAE=1.03, money-format-f1=0.96. Summary: int8 close to baseline, int4 regressed on decimal precision.

joel: Can you paste a failing example? A unique case would help.

ravi: Example A:
Prompt: "Total due: 1,234.00 USD
Apply credit: -0.50
What's remaining?"
baseline: "USD 1,233.50"
int4: "USD 1233.5" (formatting ok) but decimal drop in Example B
Example B:
Prompt: "Charges: 10 items at 0.10 each"
baseline: "USD 1.00"
int4: "USD 0.1"  (magnitude drop)

lina: That looks like exponent/scale quanta noise rather than tokenizer. Try increasing calibration samples and enabling per-channel scale (quant-opt=perchannel).

frank: Also check KV cache accumulation on long threads — small rounding can accumulate. Try rerunning long-context subset with cache disabled.

ravi: Rerunning int4 with perchannel + calib 2048 and cache disabled on long threads. Job=job_99805. Adding reproducibility metadata: model=newt-lora@v0.9, base=open-7b@2026-03-12, seed=20260323.

eval-bot: rerun complete. int4 (perchannel, calib=2048): numeric-MAE=1.08, money-format-f1=0.95. Long-thread cumulative diffs reduced. Artifacts: http://ci.internal/reports/newt/job_99805/report.html

joel: Great. Seems calibration + per-channel quant fixed majority. Recommendation: publish two artifacts: int8-general and int4-calibrated-perchannel; for customers with tight numeric constraints serve int8 or int4-calibrated-perchannel with canary limit. Add a routing tag newt-numeric-safe -> int8.

ravi: Will do. I've created canary policy in staging: if money-f1 < 0.92 on recent eval set -> route to int8 artifact. Also added rollback threshold for error-rate >3%.

lina: One more: log the failing prompts and link to ticket for adapter author to inspect soft-prompt scaling, in case underlying model behaviors are nudged. I'll open ticket ENG-ML-4321.

frank: thx. Quick nudge: add a note in run metadata about tokenizer remap for ORDR->ORDER and OOV fix so we can trace future regressions.

ravi: Done. Metadata updated and ticket created. Closing loop once production bakeout passes. :thumbsup: 

eval-bot: note: all artifacts archived to gs://redwood-artifacts/newt/job_99805/.job.tar.gz

Done.
